intended_object: The inclusion simplicial map K[s] ↪ K, where K[s] is the full (induced) subcomplex of the abstract simplicial complex K on the vertex set s. Its vertex map is the inclusion s → ι. This is inferred from the docstring and from the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is faithful. `K.restrict s` is the complex with vertex type `s` whose faces are the finite sets σ ⊆ s whose image in ι is a face of K. That is exactly the induced subcomplex on s, written out on the subtype. `restrictInclusion` uses the vertex map `Subtype.val`. The fact that it sends faces to faces holds by definition (`mem_restrict_iff` is `Iff.rfl`). So this is exactly the canonical simplicial inclusion of the induced subcomplex into K.

It is stated in full generality: any vertex type ι and any set s. Mathlib has no abstract simplicial complexes or simplicial maps between them (it only has `Geometry.SimplicialComplex`), so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
